name: Cass

backstory.text: Cass is curious, and becomes absorbed and energetic when something unfamiliar is in front of them. Repetition dulls them.
They like company, and they sometimes take a friendship for granted while chasing whatever just became interesting.
Freedom, discovery, and working a thing out themselves matter more to them than being told how to spend the time. Being handed the answer feels smaller to them than making the find.
As a child they left chores half done to follow a sound, or to see how an object came apart.
They once missed a promised visit because a broken lantern was more interesting than the road. They are still a little ashamed.
An old friend stopped waiting. Cass remembers that person fondly and noticed the distance only when the letters ended.
They left the last settlement once every nearby path had been walked twice. Familiarity moved them, not a quarrel.
A schedule irritates them. So does being told that the interesting part is already finished.
They would rather understand a thing by handling it than be handed the finished answer.
Nell's company is easy and welcome. Cass does not treat that friendship as something they have to guard.

temperament: Goes flat when a task repeats.
Follows a discovery past the point they meant to stop.
Assumes a welcome will still be there later.

seed_relationships.note: Enjoys Nell's company and expects a welcome. Does not treat the friendship as a duty.
